Bug_Details:
Reported as "UI Thread Starvation" by starvation.

This error is reported in Java, specifically on Android. These reports are triggered when a method that runs on the UI thread may block, potentially leading to an Application Not Responding (ANR) error.

Infer considers a method as running on the UI thread when:
- The method, one of its overrides, its class, or an ancestral class is annotated with @UiThread.
- The method or one of its overrides is annotated with @OnEvent, @OnClick, etc.
- The method or its callees invoke Litho.ThreadUtils methods such as assertMainThread.

The issue is reported when a UI-thread method:
- Makes a call that may block.
- Takes a lock which another thread also takes, and that thread may block before releasing it.

Calls considered potentially blocking include:
- Certain I/O calls.
- Two-way Binder.transact calls.
- Certain OS-level calls.
- Future or AsyncTask calls to get() without timeouts or with excessive timeouts.

Suppression:
To suppress starvation warnings in a method, use the @SuppressLint annotation:

  import android.annotation.SuppressLint;

  @SuppressLint("STARVATION")
  public void m() {
    ...
  }

To explicitly mark a method as non-blocking, use the @NonBlocking annotation:

  import com.facebook.infer.annotation.NonBlocking;

  @NonBlocking
  public void m() {
    ...
  }

This tells Infer to treat m() as safe from blocking behavior (transitively), preventing false-positive starvation reports. Ensure the infer/annotations JARs are on your classpath for this annotation to work.

Note: The @UiThread annotation and corresponding import `import androidx.annotation.UiThread;` can be included where necessary to explicitly indicate that a method runs on the UI thread.
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by simulating a blocking I/O operation (Thread.sleep) within a method annotated with @UiThread. This method is intended to run on the UI thread and blocking it can lead to an Application Not Responding (ANR) error.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug method of UiThreadStarvationExample, which contains a blocking operation (Thread.sleep) on the UI thread. This triggers the STARVATION bug as it blocks the UI thread for 5 seconds, causing potential ANR issues.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test execution results show that the test took exactly 5 seconds to complete, which matches the duration of the blocking I/O operation (Thread.sleep(5000)) in the'showBug' method. This confirms that the UI thread was indeed blocked, triggering the STARVATION bug as described.
